title: Finite coherent ideal filtration on a Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated; the last two conditions mean that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ for the locus of nonzero geometric stalks, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduced means that etale scheme charts have local rings without nonzero nilpotents, and irreducible means nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets. Assume $X$ is Noetherian and let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. There are an integer $m\geq0$ and a filtration by coherent submodules $$0=F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_m=F$$ such that for every $1\leq j\leq m$ there are a reduced closed subspace $i_j:Z_j\hookrightarrow X$ with $|Z_j|$ irreducible and a nonzero coherent ideal $K_j\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_j}$ satisfying $$F_j/F_{j-1}\cong(i_j)_*K_j.$$ Here direct image is [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and the quotient is the cokernel of the inclusion. The filtration may be chosen with $|i_j|(|Z_j|)=\operatorname{Supp}(F_j/F_{j-1})\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(F)$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(K_j)=|Z_j|$ for every $j$. In particular, if $\operatorname{Supp}(F)$ is empty, then $m=0$ and $F=0$.

source.place: Tag 07UR, lemma-coherent-filter, statement and proof; omit zero factors. The support control is that of the subquotients in this proof and of the nonzero ideals on reduced irreducible subspaces in Tag 07UQ, lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible.

proof.text: Filtrations concatenate across a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$: first use the filtration of $A$ inside $B$, then the inverse images $p^{-1}(C_j)$. These inverse images are the kernels of $B\to C/C_j$, hence coherent by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian]. The quotient $p^{-1}(C_j)/p^{-1}(C_{j-1})$ maps isomorphically to $C_j/C_{j-1}$: local lifts give surjectivity, and its kernel is exactly the denominator. Thus the factors are precisely those of $A$ and $C$. This also refines any finite coherent filtration once its factors have the required filtrations.

source.place: Tag 07UR, the induced-filtration argument in the reducible-support paragraph and the refinement in the ideal-power paragraph.

proof.text: Support bookkeeping will be used throughout. Restriction to an etale chart is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]; for modules this follows from sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On a locally Noetherian scheme chart, coherent Zariski kernels and cokernels exist in all modules by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Their images under the exact functor [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] are the etale kernels and cokernels. Thus the equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies coherent subquotients with Zariski subquotients. Now [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] and [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support] show that every coherent subquotient has support contained in that of its parent. A quasi-coherent module with empty support is zero: on each chart all ordinary stalks vanish, so its Zariski module is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks], then its etale restriction is zero by the equivalence. The sheaf axiom on chart coverings shows that the module is zero. Every coherent support is closed by [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], applied with $N=F$.

source.place: Tag 07UR, minimal-support choice and empty-support case; support of subquotients in every induction step, checked on etale charts.

proof.text: Fix $X$ and argue by well-founded induction on closed subsets $T\subseteq|X|$ using [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-topology]. The inductive assertion is the entire desired filtration statement for every coherent module $M$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=T$. The hypothesis is therefore available simultaneously for all modules with proper closed support in $T$. For $T=\varnothing$, Step 2 gives $M=0$ and we take $m=0$. If $T$ is nonempty and reducible, write $T=T_1\cup T_2$ with both $T_i$ proper closed. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-union-sequence] to get $0\to A\to M\to B\to0$ with supports contained in $T_1,T_2$. Their supports are closed by Step 2 and proper in $T$. The induction hypothesis supplies both filtrations, and Step 1 concatenates them. Their support control remains inside $T$.

source.place: Tag 07UR, choice of minimal bad support and the reducible-support paragraph.

proof.text: It remains to treat nonempty irreducible $T=\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. Use [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] to put the reduced closed structure $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ on $T$. The defining ideal $J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules]. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power] choose $n\geq0$ with $J^nM=0$, all $J^kM$ and $M/J^kM$ being coherent. If $n=0$ then $M=0$ and Step 2 applies. Otherwise put $P_k=J^kM/J^{k+1}M$ for $0\leq k<n$. These are coherent by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian]. Multiplication gives $JP_k=0$ since $J(J^kM)=J^{k+1}M$. Each support is contained in $T$ by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 07UR, irreducible-support and ideal-power paragraph. The displayed I in that paragraph denotes the same defining ideal as J.

proof.text: For each $P=P_k$, if its closed support is proper in $T$, use the induction hypothesis of Step 3. Otherwise $\operatorname{Supp}(P)=T$ and $JP=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-reduced-support-generic-ideal-inclusion] with this $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $P$: obtain $r\geq1$, a nonzero coherent ideal $K$ of full support on $Z$, and $0\to E\to P\to Q\to0$ where $E=i_*(K^{\oplus r})$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(Q)\subsetneq T$. All hypotheses hold because $X$ is Noetherian, $Z$ is reduced with nonempty irreducible support $T$, and $JP=0$ was proved in Step 4. The coherent $Q$ has the desired filtration by the same induction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07UR, final paragraph, applying Tag 07UQ to each full-support ideal-power factor.

proof.text: Filter $E$ by $E_t=i_*(K^{\oplus t})$ for $0\leq t\leq r$, using the first $t$ summands. The sequences $0\to K^{\oplus(t-1)}\to K^{\oplus t}\to K\to0$ split by the coordinate inclusion and projection. Exactness of closed direct image on quasi-coherent modules [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules] gives $E_t/E_{t-1}\cong i_*K$. Finite sums are coherent by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian], and the $E_t$ are coherent by [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules]. The same closed-support statement gives $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*K)=|i|(\operatorname{Supp}(K))=T$. Each factor is nonzero since this support is nonempty. Step 1 combines this filtration of $E$ with that of $Q$ to filter $P$.

source.place: Tag 07UR, final contradiction: filter the finite ideal sum by its coordinate sums, then lift the cokernel filtration.

proof.text: All $P_k$ now have the required filtrations. Refine $0=J^nM\subseteq J^{n-1}M\subseteq\cdots\subseteq JM\subseteq M$ by repeated use of Step 1. Every factor is one of the nonzero ideal direct images supplied either by the induction hypothesis or by Step 6, so its ideal has full support on its reduced irreducible closed subspace. Step 2 puts its support inside $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=T$. Delete any repeated terms in the finite refinements; their quotients are zero. This proves the induction assertion, hence the result for $M=F$, including the empty-support case already proved.

source.place: Tag 07UR, refinement of the ideal-power filtration and completion of the induction; omit zero factors.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07UR, lemma-coherent-filter, proof, with the coordinate and inverse-image refinements written out.

The reducible case uses the new union-sequence node (07UP). The irreducible case uses the reduced structure, J-adic layers from the new ideal-power node (07UK+07UD) and the new generic-inclusion node (07UQ via 08AM: JF=0 plus full support is equivalent to F=i_*G). No duplicates: the existing analogues are scheme-only (weil-pbc, pc-s3), and generic-multiple-embedding is the 07UT comparison. Declared tool uses (site restriction, Zariski kernels/stalks, trf Zariski-etale equivalence) are generic and accepted. lean.statement: theorem exists_coherent_ideal_filtration {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin (m + 1) → Subobject F) (hc : Monotone c), IsZero (c 0 : X.Modules) ∧ IsIso (c (Fin.last m)).arrow ∧ (∀ k : Fin (m + 1), SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (c k : X.Modules)) ∧ (∀ j : Fin m, ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom ∧ (∀ T : Z.EtaleSite, IsReduced (Z.etaleForget.obj T)) ∧ IrreducibleSpace (Point Z.obj.obj) ∧ ∃ K : Subobject (SheafOfModules.unit Z.structureSheaf), ¬ IsZero (K : Z.Modules) ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (K : Z.Modules) ∧ moduleSupport (K : Z.Modules) = Set.univ ∧ ∃ (Q : X.Modules) (q : (c j.succ : X.Modules) ⟶ Q) (w : Subobject.ofLE (c j.castSucc) (c j.succ) (hc j.castSucc_le_succ) ≫ q = 0), Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ q w)) ∧ Nonempty (Q ≅ (moduleDirectImage i).obj (K : Z.Modules)) ∧ pointImage i.hom.hom = moduleSupport Q ∧ moduleSupport Q ⊆ moduleSupport F) ∧ (moduleSupport F = ∅ → m = 0 ∧ IsZero F)
